summary: "Journal des Goncourt (Premier Volume)" by Edmond de Goncourt and Jules de Goncourt is a diary written collaboratively from 1850 to 1896. This candid chronicle captures the literary and artistic world of Paris, filled with bitter rivalries and volatile friendships. Through "dual dictation," the brothers recorded intimate conversations, professional jealousies, and unvarnished observations of their celebrated contemporaries—including Flaubert, Zola, Baudelaire, and Wilde. Their unflinching portraits of friends and rivals sparked controversy, strained relationships, and challenged notions of loyalty in their cutthroat cultural milieu.
